We’re grateful that SteelFab is doubling down on Cumberland.”

The Project site will be located on an approximately 409-acre area adjacent to Interstate I-20, approximately 16 miles west of Augusta, GA. The proposed Project will have a maximum capacity to process approximately 1.87 million tons of rock per year. A rock processing plant will be included in the quarry. The new permit authorizes the quarry operation after construction. The quarry will operate 12 hours per day (from 6 AM to 6 PM) ; 5 days per week; and 52 weeks per year and will use crushers and screens to obtain the required products. The roads from the quarry entrance will be paved up to approximately 700 ft. All other haul roads inside the quarry area will be unpaved. The proposed quarry operations will consist of material handling and processing (crushing and screening) operations and will generate only fugitive particulate matter (PM) emissions. Fugitive PM emissions generated from the movement of quarry rock haul trucks and customer trucks will be controlled by water spray. Fugitive PM emissions generated from the various material handling and processing operations will be controlled using water spray at all transfer points. There will be no stationary fuel combustion sources at the quarry except for the first two years or when power from the local power grid is available, whichever is earlier. The facility is classified as a synthetic minor source. The area (Columbia County) is currently in attainment for all criteria pollutants per U.S. EPA (https://www3.epa.gov/airquality/greenbook/ancl.html).
Page 2: SIP Application Review Azelea Quarry Application No. 30232 Page 2 Purpose of Application According to Application No. 30232, this new quarry will consist of pit drilling, crushing, screening, and associated material handling, storage, sale, and pollution control (wet suppression etc.). Involved process equipment/operation includes drillers, ho ppers, feeders, bins, trucks, crushers, screens, belt conveyors, stockpiles, wet suppression systems and water spray trucks. The quarry will also operate a construction aggregate/stone and sand sale operation. The operations will be powered with four Tier 4 certified diesel fired generator sets for the first two years after startup or until grid power is available, whichever is earlier. After the first two years of quarry life or less, the quarry operations will be powered by electricity from the local power grid. A public advisory was issued for this permit application.
